domain_analysis.scope: Interior new construction window sash and jamb stain and clear coat workflows
domain_analysis.workflow_overview: Three-layer coating system adapted for window assemblies: stain (color) → sanding sealer (adhesion bridge + smooth base) → clear topcoat (protection + depth). Window-specific concerns include mandatory glass masking, hardware protection, blocking prevention for operable sashes, and window_type/size_bucket rate modifiers.
key_differences_from_trim_stain: EA-based UOM (per window) instead of LF aggregate
Size_bucket modifier (S/M/L/XL) for rate scaling by window size
Mandatory glass masking (critical for stain — harder to remove than paint)
Blocking prevention critical — operable sashes must remain ajar during clear cure
Sill/stool protection when already finished by trim spec
Jamb as separate paintable item (may not be present on all windows)
key_differences_from_paint_counterpart: Bare wood input (SS_BARE) instead of primed surface
No companion prime spec — all coating layers in one spec
Three product roles (stain, sealer, clear) instead of one (finish)
Independent application method selection for stain vs clear phases
Wipe step mandatory for all stain application methods
Wood conditioner activation for softwood species
No sheen/QT gate — all clear sheens available at all tiers

zones.notes: Mandatory glass masking. Stain on glass is harder to remove than paint — careful masking critical.
Drop cloths below window. Stain drips are especially hard to clean.
Remove or mask hardware. Stain penetrates hardware finishes.
Wall masking around window. Stain on painted walls is very hard to remove.
Sill protection from overspray when stool already finished by trim spec.

analysis.interface_concern: Glass masking is the defining protection requirement. Stain penetrates glass edges more than paint.
analysis.protection_approach: Full glass masking with paper/film. No 1/16-inch seal technique for stain (that is paint-specific).

analysis.interface_concern: Window-to-wall interface. Stain on painted walls is extremely difficult to remove.
analysis.protection_approach: Wall masking for spray or when walls finished. Extra caution with stain.

analysis.interface_concern: Casing often stained with same stain/clear. Routed to SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN.
analysis.protection_approach: No protection when same finish group.

state_analysis.notes: Same state model as canonical trim stain spec. Inherited from design spec Section 7.

key_rates.sash_stain_brush_wipe: 2.5-3.0 EA/hr (M size, double-hung) — ~20-24 min per window including wipe
key_rates.sash_stain_spray_wipe: 3.5-4.0 EA/hr (M size, double-hung) — ~15-17 min per window

production_rate_analysis.comparison_to_paint: Window stain rates are comparable to paint counterpart rates. Stain includes wipe step (adds time) but no primer needed (saves a layer). Clear coat rates similar to paint finish coat rates.

risk_notes.risk: Stain bleeds onto glass through masking gaps — much harder to remove than paint
risk_notes.mitigation: Meticulous glass masking with fresh tape. No 1/16-inch seal for stain. Excess cleaned immediately.

risk_notes.risk: Clear coat bonds sash to frame if closed before full cure (3-7 days)
risk_notes.mitigation: All operable sashes remain ajar during cure. Label with 'DO NOT CLOSE' tags.

risk_notes.risk: Pine or poplar window wood absorbs stain unevenly
risk_notes.mitigation: Wood conditioner mandatory for softwood. Gel stain alternative.

risk_notes.topic: Color inconsistency between sash and jamb
risk_notes.risk: Different grain exposure or wood species between sash and jamb creates color mismatch
risk_notes.mitigation: Same stain lot, consistent application technique. Test on scrap from each component.

assumptions.value: All stain-grade windows are wood (pine, poplar, oak, cherry, walnut, mahogany). Metal and vinyl windows are not stainable.
assumptions.note: Only wood substrates in this stain spec. Paint counterpart handles wood, aluminum, steel.

assumptions.value: No 1/16-inch seal technique for stain work (that technique creates a paint-to-glass seal for water infiltration prevention). For stain, full masking to tape edge.
assumptions.note: Paint counterpart uses 1/16-inch seal per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1. Stain does not seal to glass.

assumptions.value: Size bucket modifiers for stain work: S=0.75, M=1.00, L=1.40, XL=1.80. Same as paint counterpart.
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines stain-specific size modifiers. Using paint counterpart modifiers.
